EpochParamsSummary.description: The protocol parameters a client needs to audit a published tally. Threshold lists are (name, value) pairs under db-sync's own column names, so any of them can be looked up in palmares.thresholds. `gov_action_lifetime` is the parameter, not the voting window: the ledger sets expiration = proposed_epoch + lifetime + 1.

MetricFormula.description: One published formula. `sql` is the statement the server actually executes, inlined from the same embed the query path reads, so the documented formula cannot drift from the served number. Exactly one of `sql_file` and `sql_object` is set, so every formula_id resolves to something a reader can go and look at. `params` names the positional placeholders in bind order.

StatusResponse.description: Service identity, chain freshness and protocol parameters in one request.

SyncStatus.description: How far behind the chain this index is. `lag_seconds` is measured from the tip block's time; `is_ready` is /ready's own verdict.

info.description: Read-only queries over the Cardano governance record: DReps, governance actions, votes, delegations, the constitutional committee and treasury withdrawals. Every row comes from a view over cardano-db-sync — there is no projection table and no second derivation — and every published metric carries the id of the formula that produced it, resolvable at /metrics/formulas.

get.description: Registered delegate representatives with their track record: participation, rationale coverage, vote latency, voting power, delegator count and age. Default ordering is voting_power descending, because this list is what a delegator chooses from. Statuses default to the two registered ones (active and inactive) -- preprod has 511 retired DReps against 294 registered, so including them by default would make the first page mostly useless; ask for them with status=retired. The two reserved ledger options (drep_always_abstain, drep_always_no_confidence) are never listed: they hold stake but no credential, and are published by /drep-power instead.

get.description: One action's whole record: its lifecycle, the tally per role that voted, the threshold each tally is measured against, the payments a treasury withdrawal would make, the parameters a parameter change would change, its proposer's track record, and its CIP-108 metadata -- the last only when the anchor hash verified. `basis` on every tally is `cast_votes_only`: the ratio is over the votes ACTUALLY CAST, while the ledger compares against total active voting power, so the ratio is an observation and never a prediction. `lifecycle` is the authoritative outcome. Both id forms are accepted in the path, but the canonical `<tx_hash>#<index>` contains a `#`, which a URL treats as a fragment delimiter -- it must be sent percent-encoded as `%23`. The CIP-129 `bech32` form that /gov-actions returns has no such character and is the one to put in a link.

get.description: Every governance action ever proposed, with its lifecycle. There is no default state filter, unlike /dreps: an expired action is still part of the record, and hiding 103 of preprod's 131 proposals by default would hide the history this registry exists to publish. `state` is single-valued and is a READING of the four lifecycle epochs in a fixed order, so all four travel beside it; `last_votable_epoch`, not `state`, is the authority on whether a vote is still possible. `title` and `abstract` come from CIP-108 metadata and are null for most actions -- measured, 7 of 131 on preprod have it fetched.

get.description:
Every vote cast, across all three voter roles, with the rationale anchor's outcome and the voter's power at the epoch the action's window closed. One endpoint rather than four per-actor routes: the filters are repeatable, so a DRep's record, an action's votes, a committee member's votes and the global feed are all the same query. 
`voter_id` accepts any identifier form -- drep1y…, cc_cold1…, pool1… or 56 hex characters -- and committee votes are addressed by the COLD credential, the identity that survives a hot-key rotation, with the signing hot key published beside it. 
Re-votes are returned as rows, not hidden: `revote_count` says how many exist for that (voter, action) pair and `is_final` / `is_first` mark which one a verdict or a latency is measured from. preprod's worst pair has 21,626 rows, from the epoch-187 committee stress test. 
There is no `has_rationale` parameter: it is `anchor_status=valid`, which makes the caller say which of the five anchor outcomes they mean instead of collapsing an unreachable IPFS document into "no rationale".
